🇲🇽💵 <u>PESO SHRUGS OFF TRUMP'S TARIFF THREATS — 8TH DAY UNDER 17</u>

Fresh protectionist noise from Washington and a T-MEC renegotiation grinding through its fourth round in DC, and the peso still closed Friday near 16.97 to the dollar — its eighth straight session under 17. El Financiero flagged the "risk aversion" from Trump's new tariff threats; the currency barely flinched, slipping less than half a percent on the week while holding one of its strongest levels of the year.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>"NO ELITE, NO FOREIGN GOVERNMENT WILL DECIDE MEXICO'S FUTURE"</u>

As Washington leans on Mexico in the T-MEC renegotiation and Marco Rubio claims cartels still control stretches of the country, Sheinbaum drew the line from Veracruz: "Sovereignty emanates from the people. Only the Mexican people can define their present and their future — no elite, no foreign government." Her limit in the trade talks, she said, is "sovereignty and that which we consider should not be negotiable."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>NO SECOND PASSPORT FOR MEXICO'S PRESIDENT OR GOVERNORS</u>

A constitutional reform requiring single Mexican nationality for the president, state governors and the CDMX head of government has cleared committee. Sheinbaum's logic is blunt: Mexican ambassadors already can't hold a second passport, so neither should whoever commands the country. "There are two parties that openly voted against it," she noted — the PRI and Movimiento Ciudadano — while the PAN abstained. Ordinary citizens keep their dual nationality; this touches only those who hold ultimate power.

🗳️🇲🇽 <u>INE'S EXECUTIVE SECRETARY QUITS BEFORE MEXICO'S BIGGEST-EVER VOTE</u>

Claudia Arlett Espino has resigned as Executive Secretary of Mexico's electoral authority, telling INE president Guadalupe Taddei that organizing the concurrent 2026–2027 elections "does not allow me, at this moment, to strengthen my personal and family bond." Her exit lands mid-planning for the largest electoral operation in the country's history — federal seats plus races across all 32 states, more than 21,000 posts on the ballot. She pledged to help steer the transition.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>PEMEX REFINES MORE, IMPORTS LESS</u>

Energy sovereignty in hard numbers: in July Pemex refined 418,000 barrels a day of gasoline (+20.75% over June) and 289,000 b/d of diesel (+15.1%), while gasoline imports fell to 353,000 b/d and diesel imports dropped nearly 25% in a single month. Diesel output for January–July averaged 273,000 b/d — up 37.63% from a year earlier — as the National Refining System claws back decades of deliberate neglect.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PAN GOES TO EUROPE HUNTING FOR A NEW MAXIMILIAN</u>

Five PAN leaders led by Jorge Romero are touring Europe begging for foreign backing — and Sheinbaum caught the historical rhyme instantly: when 19th-century Mexican liberals triumphed, "the conservatives, like now, went to Europe to seek support from abroad because they say there's no Mexican who can govern Mexico — and they brought Maximilian, who stayed five years, like a colony, a French protectorate." That empire ended in front of a firing squad at Querétaro in 1867.

🇲🇽📈 <u>Analysts: Mexico keeps growing, inflation eases — no recession</u>

Private-sector analysts in Citi's expectations survey see Mexico's economy growing 1.8% in 2027 with inflation cooling to 3.8%, and they nudged the 2026 growth forecast up to 1.3% — a steady, no-recession outlook even with Trump's tariffs looming, El Financiero reports.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Most Mexicans want no US troops on their soil</u>

As Washington floats "unilateral" strikes on cartels, a recent El Soberano poll finds 55% of Mexicans reject US military operations inside Mexico. It tracks President Sheinbaum's line — cooperation yes, subordination never — and a deeper reflex on the very week Mexico marks the Niños Héroes: the country that lost half its territory to a US invasion in 1847 isn't inviting the army back.

🇲🇽📉 <u>Zacatecas: daily homicides down 96% since 2021</u>

Once one of Mexico's bloodiest states, Zacatecas cut its daily homicide average 96% between 2021 and 2026 — from 4.5 killings a day to 0.2 — SESNSP chief Marcela Figueroa Franco reported. Measured just from the start of Sheinbaum's term (Sept 2024–Aug 2026) the drop is still 85%, from 1.13 to 0.17 a day. It's the lowest average in a series that reaches back to 2015.

🇲🇽💜 <u>Mexico City moves to pay for the invisible work that sustains life</u>

Women in CDMX spend up to 50 hours a week on unpaid care in the poorest households — against 14 for men — Mayor Clara Brugada said as she installed the city's Junta de Cuidados. Her program "Ciudad que Cuida a Quien Cuida" starts by paying 5,000 caregivers, most of them women, toward what she calls the "fourth R": remunerating the labor that keeps society alive — built on three aims, to desfeminize, desfamiliarize and desmercantilize care.
banner: CDMX: PAY THE INVISIBLE CARE WORK
